page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Diborane is formed
lines: boron trichloride in dry ether gives
Hydride ions transfer to boron and
chlorine to aluminium, so AlCl₃ and
steps.why: The reaction is an exchange of hydride for chloride, so naming diborane as the product and the two chlorides as the by-products states the whole change before any coefficients are worked out.
common_mistakes: Naming BH₃ as the product. Borane is not stable on its own, so two units join to give B₂H₆.
Giving LiF and AlF₃ as the by-products. Those come from the reaction with BF₃; with BCl₃ the by-products are AlCl₃ and LiCl.
steps.memory_tip: Hydrogen moves to boron, chlorine moves to aluminium and lithium.
steps.margin_note: Say dry ether. Diborane reacts with water, so the solvent has to be dry.

steps.label: Balanced equation
lines: Each side has 3 Li, 3 Al, 4 B, 12 H and
12 Cl, so the equation is balanced.
steps.why: The coefficients here are not obvious, so counting each element on both sides is the only way to be sure the equation written down is the balanced one.
common_mistakes: Writing the equation with 1 : 1 coefficients. Three LiAlH₄ and four BCl₃ are needed to match twelve hydrogen atoms with twelve chlorine atoms.
Leaving out LiCl, which leaves the lithium unaccounted for on the right.
steps.memory_tip: The coefficients read 3, 4, 2, 3, 3 in the order they are written.
steps.margin_note: Write dry ether above the arrow and the word warm beside it.

insider_note: The balanced equation carries this answer, so write it in full and name the two chlorides; a single line saying only that diborane forms leaves the change half stated.
